Class RcxFirmware

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.remote.lego.rcx.RcxFirmware
public final class RcxFirmware extends Object
Loads firmware into an RCX brick over infrared, as the LEGO IR tower does: the brick's boot ROM answers these four commands even when it has no firmware, which is the state it is in after its batteries were out (the display then shows program 0). Get it from RemoteRcx.getFirmware() after constructing the RcxLink with both the IR LED and the IR receiver module, since every step waits for the brick's reply.

The sequence is delete(), start(int, int) with the image's entry address and checksum, one successful transfer(int, byte[], int) per block of up to 200 bytes numbered from 1, then unlock(); a 16 KB image takes about three minutes at 2400 baud. The RcxLink is configured before this loader is created.

  • Method Details

    • installed

      public int installed()
      Asks the brick for its versions: 1 when it runs firmware, 0 when only its boot ROM runs (so it ignores motor, sensor and sound commands until firmware is loaded), or NO_REPLY. The boot ROM answers this too, so it tells a brick without firmware from one out of range.

    • delete

      public boolean delete()
      Deletes the firmware the brick holds, if any. Returns whether the brick acknowledged.

    • start

      public boolean start(int entryAddress, int checksum)
      Announces an image that will run from entryAddress, whose bytes below CHECKSUM_END add up to checksum (modulo 65536). Returns whether the brick acknowledged.

    • transfer

      public int transfer(int index, byte[] block, int length)
      Sends block number index (1 for the first) holding the first length bytes of block (at most 200), once; a full block takes about two seconds. Returns the brick's status, 0 when it stored the block, NO_REPLY when no answer came, or the brick's error code. The caller may retry the identical block, but the boot ROM mishandles duplicate firmware transfers: repeated missing replies require restarting the download, never assuming the block was stored. Use index 0 for the final block; it finalizes the image checksum and cannot be retransmitted.

    • unlock

      public boolean unlock()
      Starts the downloaded firmware once the brick has checked it. The brick answers with a long text that this receiver does not decode, so the call only reports whether any answer arrived; that the firmware runs shows on the brick's display (program 1) and in RcxBrick commands being acknowledged.
